scope: Source-only review of eight-file RECOVERY-RESTORE-EDIT repair and twelve new controlled regression cases. No complete feature approval or new runtime evidence.

evidence: RecoveryWorkspace.restore owns the same view before its first await, waits the existing checkpoint chain, remembers the listed committed draft version, and checks active plugin/current namespace/generation after reads.

Lease captures the complete editable draft fingerprint, including text, intent, profile, ordered references, attachments and steering. New-chat project/title remain editable; existing center-owned project display fields are excluded from the fingerprint and App independently checks the saved project envelope against the loaded conversation.

changed() records interleaved modifications instead of discarding them. Invalidated remains set through edit-then-revert. lease.check after projection.refresh rejects late application; same-view second Restore and beginHandoff are rejected during the first restore.

App initial material guard now includes intent/profile-only, steering and unprepared project selections. Real App and tests consume restoreConversationDraft for awaited refresh followed by lease recheck and synchronous preparation/application.

Knowledge, attachment and steering owners prepare synchronous validation before any selected material/editor commit. Steering identity, authorization, duplicate keys, existing drafts and capacity are checked before field application. No new HTTP command or controller authority is introduced.

After conflict/success the restore lease is removed and the current complete draft is checkpointed through the original stable owner/slot/version CAS. Offline edits retain captured namespace plus a visible checkpoint error until same-namespace reauthentication; storage failures retain memory. The accepted CAS clarification allows ordinary successful new-draft checkpoint to replace the one slot.
